title: 🐉J.F. Bierlein on Poetry, Myth, and Metaphor -www.gettherapybirmingham.com

sentences.en: That boy needs therapy.
sentences.zh: 那小子需要治疗。

sentences.en: Lie down on the couch.
sentences.zh: 躺到沙发上。

sentences.en: Well, we'll just go ahead and start where I can introduce you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们直接开始，我来给你做个介绍。

sentences.en: So I'm here with J.F.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我和J.F.在一起。

sentences.en: Barrelane.
sentences.zh: 巴雷兰。

sentences.en: Am I saying that correctly?
sentences.zh: 我没念错吧？

sentences.en: Close enough.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: Normally, I kind of maybe over-prepare for these, but it's been such a crazy week.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，我对这些节目可能准备得有点过头了，但这周实在太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I've rescheduled three times, and I don't have a ton of structure to the interview.
sentences.zh: 我改期了三次，这次采访也没什么太多结构。

sentences.en: But I think the themes are going to be mythology and poetry.
sentences.zh: 但我认为主题会围绕神话和诗歌展开。

sentences.en: Because you're a scholar and a poet and a gentleman.
sentences.zh: 因为你既是学者、诗人，也是位绅士。

sentences.en: Anything else?
sentences.zh: 还有别的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, golly.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: You're too generous.
sentences.zh: 你太抬举我了。

sentences.en: I think it's really fun because I just want to give a little background.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很有趣，因为我只想做点背景介绍。

sentences.en: Joel was very kind when he contacted me.
sentences.zh: 乔尔联系我的时候非常客气。

sentences.en: He said, you know, I read your books when I was a kid, which made me feel ancient, of course, and really enjoyed them.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我小时候读过你的书——当然这让我觉得自己老态龙钟了——而且真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: And it's so funny because I always spend time discussing my books and, you know, I wrote them 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这太搞笑了，因为我总是花时间讨论我的书，而你知道的，那些是我30年前写的。

sentences.en: And this is my OCD site where I say, I found the following errors in them.
sentences.zh: 这是我的强迫症专栏，我在上面说，我在里面发现了以下错误。

sentences.en: And it's really funny because I got some contact back from people saying, you know, great book, but this was wrong.
sentences.zh: 真的很好笑，因为我收到了一些人的反馈，他们说，书是好书，但这里错了。

sentences.en: And I would write back and say, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 然后我会回信说，你完全说得对。

sentences.en: And the three examples I give are, I was all excited because the city of Mars, Pennsylvania, I thought, ah, it's named after the Roman God.
sentences.zh: 我举的三个例子是：我当时超级兴奋，因为宾夕法尼亚州的马尔斯市，我心想，啊，它是以罗马神话中的战神命名的。

sentences.en: No, never a man named Mars.
sentences.zh: 不，从来没有一个叫马尔斯的人。

sentences.en: Maybe he was named after the Roman God.
sentences.zh: 也许它是以罗马神命名的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it might be.
sentences.zh: 对，也许是的。

sentences.en: And then the other one I thought was pretty funny was London, the city of London.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个我觉得挺搞笑的是伦敦，伦敦市。

sentences.en: I don't know where I got this from.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个说法是从哪听来的。

sentences.en: Oh, it was named after the Celtic God, Luke.
sentences.zh: 哦，它是以凯尔特神卢克命名的。

sentences.en: And about eight people said, oh, from Britain, of course, said, where did you get that crazy idea?
sentences.zh: 大约有八个人——当然都是英国人——说，你从哪听来的这种荒谬想法？

sentences.en: It's that was another one.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个例子。

sentences.en: It's Londonium, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是朗蒂尼姆（Londinium），对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I love Londonium for it, but yes.
sentences.zh: 对，我很喜欢朗蒂尼姆这个说法，但确实如此。

sentences.en: And then the third one, which is the one I blush when I admit to, is hetero in Greek means other, right?
sentences.zh: 然后第三个，让我承认时都脸红的错误是，希腊语里的“hetero”意思是“其他”，对吧？

sentences.en: But hetaira means a courtesan.
sentences.zh: 但“hetaira”的意思是交际花。

sentences.en: And so hetairism, I had read it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 所以关于“hetairism”（妾制），我以前在别的地方读过不同的解释。

sentences.en: And what I was saying was the period of hetairism was, I believe, the period of life analogous to the courtesans.
sentences.zh: 我当时说的是，妾制的时期，我认为是类似于交际花的生活时期。

sentences.en: And I missed that completely, right over my, right past my vision.
sentences.zh: 我完全漏掉了这一点，它就这么从我眼皮底下滑过去了。

sentences.en: But I cannot start an interview without, you know, confessing those three mistakes.
sentences.zh: 但我如果不先坦白这三个错误，就没法开始采访。

sentences.en: And somebody asked me, well, if you feel that way, then the rest of your book must be pretty good.
sentences.zh: 有人问我，好吧，如果你这么觉得，那你的书的其他部分一定相当不错。

sentences.en: And I said, well, I hope so, you know.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，希望如此吧。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, it's always normal to make mistakes when you're compiling anything that's the size of a book.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，当你整理一整本书这么大体量的东西时，犯错是很正常的。

sentences.en: But also, you know, it's going to be in anything.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，任何东西里都会有错。

sentences.en: But I think what made your books better is that they're not strictly academic.
sentences.zh: 不过我觉得让你的书更好的地方在于，它们不完全是学术性的。

sentences.en: They're about very intelligent concepts, but they're not pretentious.
sentences.zh: 它们探讨的是非常深刻的概念，但并不矫情。

sentences.en: And there isn't that, not even pretension, but there's an academic type of writing where you can tell that someone is used to somebody behind them being like, oh,
sentences.zh: 而且没有那种——甚至都不是矫情，而是一种学术腔的写作，你能看出作者习惯了身后有人在盯着说，哦，

sentences.en: you didn't cite your source.
sentences.zh: 你没标明引用来源。

sentences.en: How do you know that emotion comes from, you know, you're like, okay, just sit with the metaphor for a minute, man.
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道那种情绪来自于……你知道的，你会想：行吧，老兄，先感受一下这个隐喻行吗。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not trying.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不是在试图……

sentences.en: And you can tell that there's some people that when they're writing,
sentences.zh: 你能看出有些人他们在写作时，

sentences.en: they're trying to qualify everything and lay out these terms and define what the terms mean and explain why they're there before they say anything.
sentences.zh: 总是试图在说任何话之前，先把所有东西都加上限定条件，摆出这些术语，定义它们的含义，并解释它们为什么存在。

sentences.en: And it makes the books kind of a miserable read, you know.
sentences.zh: 这让阅读这些书成了一种痛苦的体验，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like, academic writing has its purpose, but the purpose is research.
sentences.zh: 比如说，学术写作有它的用处，但它的用处在于研究。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 而不是……

sentences.en: Well, you know, it's funny you should say that because all of the myths I cite in my books, I always have, you know, references in the back of the book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，你这么说挺有意思的，因为我在书里引用的所有神话，书后都有参考文献。

sentences.en: So if someone wants to know, they can look.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人想知道，他们可以去查。

sentences.en: But what I've found most useful is, and this is a result of exactly what you're talking about, is reading works saying, you know, a lot of people I talk to say, well,
sentences.zh: 但我发现最有用的是——这正是你刚才所说的结果——在阅读作品时，许多和我交流的人会说，

sentences.en: you just tell me what the heck this myth says.
sentences.zh: 你直接告诉我这个神话到底在讲什么不就完了。

sentences.en: What is the story?
sentences.zh: 故事是什么？

sentences.en: What is the narrative?
sentences.zh: 叙事是什么？

sentences.en: And, you know, I found that that people got more out of it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我发现人们从中收获更多。

sentences.en: And then what's really interesting is they ask more important questions.
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是，他们会提出更重要的问题。

sentences.en: And by important questions, I mean not just about the meaning of the myth, but how the myth informs their sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 我所说的重要问题，不仅指神话的含义，还指神话如何塑造他们对意义的理解。

sentences.en: And that, I thought, was a much better approach than being too dry and academic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这比过于枯燥和学术化的方法要好得多。

sentences.en: And because that's kind of where I was trying to take people, you know that from reading my books, but to contemplate.
sentences.zh: 因为那正是我试图引导人们去做的方向，读过我书的人都知道这一点，那就是去沉思。

sentences.en: And what was it, the Chinese philosopher Moses used to say that, you know, you can't learn anything without self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 中国哲学家墨子（注：此处原文误将老子或墨子记为Moses，译者按原意处理）不是说过吗，不经自我反思，你就什么也学不到。

sentences.en: Well, when you read a myth, it's got to be like, how does this affect me?
sentences.zh: 好吧，当你阅读一个神话时，你必须思考：这对我有什么影响？

sentences.en: What does it sense on my meaning?
sentences.zh: 它对我的意义感意味着什么？

sentences.en: And I, that's kind of where I was coming from.
sentences.zh: 我，我就是从这个角度出发的。

sentences.en: Well, I plagiarized some of it, I think, in like sixth grade for a sermon because it was like a youth Sunday or whatever.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我在六年级左右曾为了布道抄袭过一些内容，因为当时是什么青年主日之类的活动。

sentences.en: And you had to give the sermon at the Episcopal Church.
sentences.zh: 你必须在圣公会教堂做布道。

sentences.en: And I was doing something about sitting in the imagery of the Bible or sitting in the imagery of the story.
sentences.zh: 我当时在讲一些关于沉浸在圣经意象中或者沉浸在故事意象中的事情。

sentences.en: And you had a chapter about water and, you know, water showing up in myths and all these facts about water.
sentences.zh: 你有一章关于水的内容，你知道的，水在神话中出现，还有关于水的所有这些事实。

sentences.en: And I remember copying and pasting a lot of lines from that into the sermon.
sentences.zh: 我记得把里面很多行复制粘贴到了布道词里。

sentences.en: So your words have come from the pulpit too.
sentences.zh: 所以你的话也从布道坛上传播过。

sentences.en: Well, the statute of limitations is out, so I'm not going to bother you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，追诉期已过，所以我就不跟你计较了。

sentences.en: I didn't make any money off the sermon.
sentences.zh: 我从那次布道里可没赚到钱。

sentences.en: No, there you go.
sentences.zh: 不，这就对了。

sentences.en: That's the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这么回事。

sentences.en: But it's pretty funny, though, when I hear people have quoted me and so on.
sentences.zh: 不过挺搞笑的，每当我听说有人引用过我之类的话。

sentences.en: The most, a couple of really funny things, before I get into some other, my later work is what I've been doing.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的几件事——在我聊到其他事情、我后期的工作之前——

sentences.en: A couple of great funny stories to tell is I'm more popular in Brazil than I am in the United States.
sentences.zh: 有几个很棒的趣事要分享，那就是我在巴西比在美国更受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I find this totally funny because they sold the Portuguese rights and I speak and read Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 我发现这太搞笑了，因为他们卖出了葡萄牙语版权，而我会说也会读葡萄牙语。

sentences.en: So I got to read the manuscript, which is pretty cool, and make my little, you know, notes and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以我得以阅读手稿，这真的很酷，还可以做点自己的小笔记什么的。

sentences.en: And I started getting calls for interviews with outlets in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始接到巴西媒体采访的电话。

sentences.en: And what was funny was, and they knew I spoke Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们知道我会说葡萄牙语。

sentences.en: So it was really funny.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And at one point, I think it was, my sales in Brazil were higher than they were in the United States and Canada.
sentences.zh: 而且有一段时间，我想我在巴西的销量比在美国和加拿大的还要高。

sentences.en: It happens.
sentences.zh: 这种事确实会发生。

sentences.en: It happens.
sentences.zh: 这很正常。

sentences.en: You hit the Z-geast of some other country, like Japan.
sentences.zh: 你契合了某个国家（比如日本）的时代精神。

sentences.en: A lot of times, something will blow up there, you know, 10 years later or something.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，有些东西会在那里突然大火，你知道的，是在10年之后什么的。

sentences.en: I think it's Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我想是巴西。

sentences.en: It's some South American country.
sentences.zh: 是某个南美国家。

sentences.en: But there was this show that was, like, on APT, just Alabama Public Television when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 但我小时候，有一个节目在APT上播过，也就是阿拉巴马公共电视台。

sentences.en: And it was, like, a weirder version of Bill Nye the Science Guy.
sentences.zh: 它就像是《比尔·奈科学小子》的一个更古怪的版本。

sentences.en: It's called Beekman's World.
sentences.zh: 它叫《比克曼的世界》。

sentences.en: So there'd be a guy that was, like, in a rat costume, and they would do science experiments.
sentences.zh: 所以里面会有一个穿着老鼠服装的人，他们会做科学实验。

sentences.en: But it was, like, real wacky.
sentences.zh: 但它是那种超级疯狂的风格。

sentences.en: So for some reason, that is still, you know, no one even remembers it here.
sentences.zh: 所以也不知为什么，虽然这里甚至没人记得它了，

sentences.en: For some reason, it's, like, huge in this South American country.
sentences.zh: 但不知为何，它在那个南美国家非常火爆。

sentences.en: It's, like, still on TV being rerun.
sentences.zh: 它现在还在电视上重播。

sentences.en: And the guy, like, went to live there because he's basically a celebrity in this country.
sentences.zh: 那个家伙甚至搬到那里去住了，因为他在那个国家简直是个名流。

sentences.en: But it's a show to teach kids science.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个教孩子们科学的节目。

sentences.en: It's weird.
sentences.zh: 这很诡异。

sentences.en: But, you know, it spoke to something in the culture.
sentences.zh: 不过，它确实触动了当地文化中的某些东西。

sentences.en: Oh, very strange.
sentences.zh: 哦，太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I love stuff like that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我挺喜欢这种事的。

sentences.en: That is fun.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: But, yeah, go ahead, sir.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，请继续，先生。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请。

sentences.en: Well, I guess just so for the listeners to introduce you, you know, we've been wanting to talk for a while.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想为了向听众介绍你，你知道的，我们一直想聊聊。

sentences.en: So probably want to qualify so other people can understand the conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以可能需要做点铺垫，好让其他人能理解这段对话。

sentences.en: You know, I'm a therapist now.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我现在是一名治疗师。

sentences.en: I write a lot about myth and psychology and the fusion of those things and religion and Jung.
sentences.zh: 我写了很多关于神话、心理学以及这两者的融合、宗教和荣格的文章。

sentences.en: And a lot of that, I think, you know, I was born in 87.
sentences.zh: 我想其中很大一部分，你知道的，我是87年出生的。

sentences.en: But I think it was still in the water from the 70s, the Joseph Campbell stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得70年代的空气中依然弥漫着约瑟夫·坎贝尔的影响。

sentences.en: And so I read a lot of, like, science fiction and fantasy, but I didn't really read a lot of nonfiction.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了很多科幻和奇幻小说，但其实没读太多非虚构作品。

sentences.en: And then it was in fifth or sixth grade, and a friend of our family gave me, like, a gift certificate to the bookstore.
sentences.zh: 然后在我上五年级或六年级的时候，我们家的一位朋友送了我一张书店的礼品卡。

sentences.en: So I went and picked your book out because I opened it to the story of the Hindu pantheon where I don't have the book on me.
sentences.zh: 于是我去了，挑了你的书，因为我翻到了印度万神殿的故事那一页——我身上没带那本书。

sentences.en: But somebody goes to talk to the god, and he's like, how many gods are there?
sentences.zh: 但有人去跟神对话，他问：有多少个神？

sentences.en: And they're like, well, there's 130.
sentences.zh: 他们回答说：嗯，有130个。

sentences.en: And he's like, yeah, but really, how many are they?
sentences.zh: 他又问：好吧，但实际上到底有多少个？

sentences.en: And they're like, well, they share an aspect.
sentences.zh: 他们回答：嗯，他们共享一个面向。

sentences.en: There's really 50.
sentences.zh: 实际上只有50个。

sentences.en: And he's like, no, but really, how many are there?
sentences.zh: 他说：不，但实际上到底有多少个？

sentences.en: And he's like, well, there's three.
sentences.zh: 他们回答：嗯，有3个。

sentences.en: It's like, well, how many are there?
sentences.zh: 他又问：那到底有多少个？

sentences.en: And it's like, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 然后对方说：好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: You got me.
sentences.zh: 你把我问住了。

sentences.en: It's really, I'm in all of them.
sentences.zh: 其实，我存在于所有这些神之中。

sentences.en: Like, there's really just one, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像，实际上只有一个神，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And it was like, and I started thinking about the way that religion, there's a universalness to it, but then there's also something that's very, like, culturally unique.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始思考宗教的方式：它既有一种普遍性，但同时又具有非常独特的文化特征。

sentences.en: And then it's this, people are talking about basically their life and their existence in a unique voice, but they're all describing the same thing,
sentences.zh: 然后就是，人们用独特的声音谈论着他们的生活和存在，但他们其实都在描述同一件事，

sentences.en: even though I don't really like the comparative religion trope that all religions are the same.
sentences.zh: 尽管我其实并不喜欢那种“所有宗教都一样”的比较宗教学陈词滥调。

sentences.en: I don't think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是真的。

sentences.en: And it was like, just opened this door of, like, what comparative religion was and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 这就好比打开了一扇门，让我了解什么是比较宗教学以及所有这些内容。

sentences.en: And I started getting into that, and I read about mythology and all these things forever.
sentences.zh: 我开始深入研究，并永远地迷上了神话和这些事物。

sentences.en: And people would always be like, well, Joel likes history, so he's reading these stories.
sentences.zh: 人们总是会说，哦，乔尔喜欢历史，所以他在读这些故事。

sentences.en: And I was like, it's not history.
sentences.zh: 而我会说：这不是历史。

sentences.en: It's psychology, you know?
sentences.zh: 这是心理学，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, but no one really got that, and it really opened a door.
sentences.zh: 但是没有人真正理解这一点，而它确实打开了一扇门。

sentences.en: So it's exciting to talk to you now and see.
sentences.zh: 所以现在能和你交谈并看到这一切，我感到很兴奋。

sentences.en: So what brought you to wanting to write about mythology and doing those books?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么促使你想去写神话并创作那些书的呢？

sentences.en: We have them in our professional library at work, and we let patients and clinicians borrow them.
sentences.zh: 我们单位的专业图书馆里有你的书，我们允许病人和临床医生借阅。

sentences.en: And I tried to grab both of them, and they were both checked out.
sentences.zh: 我本想把那两本都拿过来，结果都被借出去了。

sentences.en: So hopefully we'll get them back.
sentences.zh: 所以希望我们能把它们要回来。

sentences.en: Well, that's a great introduction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真是一个很好的介绍。

sentences.en: I've always been a person who loved to read stories.
sentences.zh: 我一直是一个喜欢读故事的人。

sentences.en: I was kind of a, I guess you'd say, introverted, introspective kid.
sentences.zh: 我算是一个，你想怎么说都行，内向、爱反省的孩子。

sentences.en: And I remember one time my parents, I think they wanted to shut me up.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我的父母，我想他们是想让我闭嘴。

sentences.en: So they said, let's give this kid a book and leave us alone.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，给这孩子一本书，然后别来烦我们。

sentences.en: And the book was a mythology book.
sentences.zh: 然后那本书是一本神话书。

sentences.en: And I got into it, and that's probably about, I would say, oh, 10 or 11.
sentences.zh: 我迷上了它，当时我大概，我想想，哦，10岁或11岁。

sentences.en: And it was a mythology for children.
sentences.zh: 那是一本写给儿童的神话书。

sentences.en: And it was Greek and Roman mythology and some Norse.
sentences.zh: 里面有希腊、罗马神话，还有一些北欧神话。

sentences.en: And then I said, this is really good stuff, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，这真是好东西，你知道的。

sentences.en: My grandparents then said, oh, that's, my grandparents said, oh, this is the birth of an intellectual experience for this child.
sentences.zh: 我祖父母当时就说，哦，那是，我祖父母说，哦，这对这孩子来说是一次知识体验的萌芽。

sentences.en: So they decided that they would festoon me with books, all which I read.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定用书把我围起来，这些书我都读了。

sentences.en: And then when I was in college and taking a course, I had a wonderful professor.
sentences.zh: 然后当我在大学里上一门课时，我遇到了一位极好的教授。

sentences.en: And this guy and I, I'll give a shout out to the late Theodore Ludwig.
sentences.zh: 这家伙和我——我要向已故的西奥多·路德维希致敬。

sentences.en: And this guy and I could talk for hours about mythology.
sentences.zh: 这家伙和我可以连续几个小时谈论神话。

sentences.en: And he was a fascinating guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个极有魅力的人。

sentences.en: He was a Lutheran pastor and a theologian and a scholar of mythology and all these things.
sentences.zh: 他是一位路德宗牧师、神学家、神话学者，集诸多身份于一身。

sentences.en: And he said, you know what you need to do?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道你需要做什么吗？

sentences.en: You need to go, you need to get a copy of The Golden Bough by Frasier.
sentences.zh: 你需要去，你需要弄一本弗雷泽写的《金枝》。

sentences.en: And go sit on the beach sometime, just read.
sentences.zh: 找个时间去海滩坐坐，读一读就行了。

sentences.en: And I did that.
sentences.zh: 我照做了。

sentences.en: And then it was the whole obsession I had with what are the common things that make us tick?
sentences.zh: 然后我就开始痴迷于那些让我们运转的共同事物到底是什么？

sentences.en: All human beings have stuff that makes them tick.
sentences.zh: 所有人类都有让他们运转的内在驱动力。

sentences.en: And mythology kind of is a record of that search for meaning and what makes us tick and a reflection of it at the same time that makes some sense.
sentences.zh: 神话在某种程度上就是对这种寻找意义以及让我们运转的事物的记录，同时也是一种富有意义的映照。

sentences.en: And so I thought that was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And so I just continued to read and everything else in my, my addiction to languages and also helped me out because I was able to then look at some, you know,
sentences.zh: 于是我继续阅读，我生活中的其他一切——我对语言的沉迷也帮了我大忙，因为这让我能够去查看一些，你知道的，

sentences.en: even some primary sources with three dictionaries and a magnifying glass.
sentences.zh: 甚至借助三本字典和一个放大镜去阅读一些第一手资料。

sentences.en: So you don't think I'm that clever.
sentences.zh: 免得你觉得我有多聪明似的。

sentences.en: How many languages do you speak?
sentences.zh: 你会说多少种语言？

sentences.en: You were speaking like in three or four different languages when we were on the phone telling a story about going to South America.
sentences.zh: 当我们通电话讲去南美洲的故事时，你好像用了三四种不同的语言。

sentences.en: Oh, how many languages are you fluent in enough?
sentences.zh: 哦，你流利掌握的语言有几种？

sentences.en: Uh, you know, I'm picking up English pretty well.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，我英语学得挺不错的。

sentences.en: Uh, but actually my latest thing is, is Turkish.
sentences.zh: 呃，不过实际上我最近在学的是土耳其语。

sentences.en: I really enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's not in New York and we've made three trips to Turkey.
sentences.zh: 它不在纽约，我们已经去过土耳其三次了。

sentences.en: I have, I'm going to give a shout out to my wonderful Turkish teacher in Istanbul, Seda Shirel.
sentences.zh: 我要向我在伊斯坦布尔的优秀土耳其语老师塞达·希雷尔致敬。

sentences.en: And, uh, and, you know, and you can watch all those great Turkish soap operas and understand them now without subtitles, which, which is great.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道的，你现在可以看所有那些精彩的土耳其肥皂剧，不用字幕就能看懂，这真的太棒了。

sentences.en: And by the way, if you want to talk about archetypes, okay, I'm going to tell you, if you want to know what an archetype is,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你想聊聊原型，好吧，我告诉你，如果你想知道什么是原型，

sentences.en: I will use Turkish drama as a way to explain what archetypes are.
sentences.zh: 我将用土耳其电视剧作为例子来解释什么是原型。

sentences.en: Every Turkish drama has the kindly and innocent, uh, young lady who is being abused by a wrathful father and or mother.
sentences.zh: 每一部土耳其电视剧里都有一个善良无辜的年轻女孩，她正遭受着暴怒的父亲或母亲的虐待。

sentences.en: Then there's always the sweet old lady who's the cleaning woman, but knows all of their dirty secrets.
sentences.zh: 然后总会有一个慈祥的老太太作为清洁工，但她知道所有人见不得光的秘密。

sentences.en: And then there's always the dashing, but poor young man who's the hero.
sentences.zh: 接着总会有一个风度翩翩但很穷的年轻男子作为英雄。

sentences.en: And there's always some vile, vile, rich, spoiled brat kid and his rotten parents and Disney movie.
sentences.zh: 而且总有一些邪恶至极、富有、被宠坏的熊孩子和他那烂透了的父母，就像迪士尼电影一样。

sentences.en: Oh, it's, it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实是。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, Hallmark, uh, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，霍尔马克公司，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Well, it's so funny as if, you know, someone were to ask me, what is an archetype?
sentences.zh: 好吧，很有意思的是，如果有人问我，什么是原型？

sentences.en: I'd say, watch a Turkish drama, actually probably any soap opera.
sentences.zh: 我会说，去看一部土耳其电视剧，其实可能随便哪部肥皂剧都行。

sentences.en: And you find the same type of characters.
sentences.zh: 你都会发现同一类型的角色。

sentences.en: And I said, really, that is what goes on a myth.
sentences.zh: 我说，真的，神话里讲的就是这个。

sentences.en: You've got very much this, these archetypes and where do they come from?
sentences.zh: 你非常深刻地拥有这些原型，它们从何而来？

sentences.en: Well, Jung tells us that they're images in our collective unconscious, uh, but it's, they occur everywhere.
sentences.zh: 嗯，荣格告诉我们，它们是我们集体无意识中的意象，呃，但它们无处不在。

sentences.en: They're fascinating because they occur in every culture.
sentences.zh: 它们很迷人，因为它们出现在每一种文化中。

sentences.en: And that was another thing that fascinated me in reading the myths that they, you know, some of the plots, even I get one of my books.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在阅读神话时另一个让我着迷的地方，它们，你知道的，有些情节，甚至我在我的一本书里也写过。

sentences.en: I say there's a Blackfoot American Indian story that matches to an Egyptian story.
sentences.zh: 我说有一个黑脚印第安人故事与一个埃及故事相吻合。

sentences.en: I mean, that matches to a Bible story, but the Bible story and the Egyptian story, eh, they were neighbors, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它与一个圣经故事相吻合，但圣经故事和埃及故事，呃，它们是邻居，对吧？

sentences.en: But the Blackfoot are out in the middle of the, uh, North America.
sentences.zh: 但黑脚族远在北美洲中部。

sentences.en: And it's just all of the material is there.
sentences.zh: 所有这些素材就在那里。

sentences.en: And Lebi Strauss and the structuralists, they, they love that stuff.
sentences.zh: 列维-斯特劳斯和结构主义者，他们，他们非常喜欢这些东西。

sentences.en: But, but I always felt that it's a sense of meaning is what that's about.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是我一直觉得，这关乎一种意义感。

sentences.en: So, that we all, human beings, you know, we're in this time now where people are all tribal and they don't necessarily.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所有人，人类，你知道的，我们现在处于这样一个时代，人们都极具部落主义色彩，他们不一定……

sentences.en: Well, they're still fighting about myths, you know, they're fighting about mythology.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们仍在为神话争吵，你知道的，他们在为神话争吵。

sentences.en: I was going to say, they don't share myths, but common myths, and they don't see the commonality of other people's myths or the commonality of other people.
sentences.zh: 我本来想说，他们不分享神话，而是不分享共同的神话，他们看不到别人神话的共性，也看不到其他人身上的共性。

sentences.en: And, you know, this creates strife and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这造成了冲突以及所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And I, of course, you know, as, as you do, we try to lessen others' suffering and try to make life a little better for people.
sentences.zh: 而我，当然，你知道，正如你所做的那样，我们试图减少他人的痛苦，试图让人们的生活变得更好一点。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things I think you can do through the study of myths is you start saying, ah, I am, I have cultural differences, but the me,
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以通过研究神话做到这一点，那就是你开始说，啊，我，我有文化差异，但这个我，

sentences.en: what makes me tick is a lot like every other person out there in this world.
sentences.zh: 让我运转的动力其实与这世上的其他每个人非常相似。

sentences.en: And that will change how I view and treat other people.
sentences.zh: 这会改变我看待和对待其他人的方式。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting with the, the, doing a podcast that's kind of rooted in brain-based medicine and depth psychology is like Jungian, the Jungian stuff in the depth psychology,
sentences.zh: 好吧，有趣的是，做一档根植于脑科学和深度心理学的播客，就像荣格学派的东西，深度心理学中的荣格学派内容，

sentences.en: like it informs everything.
sentences.zh: 它为一切提供了指引。

sentences.en: So, it's like we talk to musicians and architects and urban planners.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们和音乐家、建筑师、城市规划师交谈。

sentences.en: A guy reached out after our urban planner documentary and he was like, or after our urban planning interview with Andres Twani,
sentences.zh: 在我们推出城市规划纪录片之后，或者在我们对安德雷斯·杜瓦尼进行城市规划采访之后，有人联系了我，

sentences.en: somebody sent me their manuscript that now is getting published, which is, I'm proud of him.
sentences.zh: 有人给我发了他们的手稿，现在这本书要出版了，我为他感到骄傲。

sentences.en: And maybe he'll be on here one day, but he had written a book about using Jungian mysticism to do urban planning,
sentences.zh: 也许有一天他会来到这里，但他写了一本关于利用荣格神秘主义来进行城市规划的书，

sentences.en: like how to find the archetypes of the way that people want to interact with a design space.
sentences.zh: 比如如何找到人们想要与设计空间进行互动的那些原型。

sentences.en: So, it's, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: And all this, there's a lot of things in Jungianism that are just everyday life.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，荣格学派中有很多东西其实就是日常生活。

sentences.en: You just say, aha, that's it.
sentences.zh: 你只会说，啊哈，原来如此。

sentences.en: I'm not going to get into a long discussion, but I mean, there's archetypalism, but also animus anima, the shadow, all these things you see manifested and view more than I am,
sentences.zh: 我不想展开长篇大论，但我的意思是，有原型主义，还有阿尼姆斯与阿尼玛、阴影，所有这些你在生活中看到显现的事物，比我看到的要多得多，

sentences.en: sure.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定。

sentences.en: But you see it manifested all over the place and they kind of help you navigate a little bit, I feel.
sentences.zh: 但你看到它们到处都在显现，我觉得它们能在一定程度上指引你前行。

sentences.en: What's a lens that lets you understand yourself and other people in a way that is gentler, I think?
sentences.zh: 这是一种能让你以更温和的方式理解自己和他人的视角，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And you can navigate life better, I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你可以更好地驾驭生活。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, navigate with that sense of meaning that I think everything boils down to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，带着那种我认为一切归根结底的意义感去前行。

sentences.en: So, you started reading mythology as a kid.
sentences.zh: 所以，你从小就开始读神话。

sentences.en: Did you ever get into psychology or you stayed in myth?
sentences.zh: 你有没有涉足过心理学，还是只专注于神话？

sentences.en: I mean, what did your academic or what did your track look like as a professional?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你的学术轨迹或者作为专业人士的轨迹是怎样的？

sentences.en: I really don't want to go into it.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想深入谈这个。

sentences.en: I don't want to do too much because now I'm working in a consulting firm.
sentences.zh: 我不想讲太多，因为现在我在一家咨询公司工作。

sentences.en: We manage contracts for companies to visit with the federal government.
sentences.zh: 我们为公司管理与联邦政府进行拜访的合同。

sentences.en: But I went into political science and economics and I was teaching as an adjunct in the Washington semester program at American University.
sentences.zh: 但我学的是政治学和经济学，我曾在美利坚大学的华盛顿学期项目中担任兼职讲师。

sentences.en: And I always tell people my night job was mythology that I, you know, read and did so many things.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉别人，我的夜间工作就是神话，我，你知道的，阅读并做了很多事情。

sentences.en: And I've had a couple of people who are true scholars, which I didn't claim to be in the field, contact me.
sentences.zh: 我有几个真正的学者——我并不自诩为该领域的学者——联系了我。

sentences.en: And they said, you know, we like your book or we're interested in your ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，我们喜欢你的书，或者我们对你的观点很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So, and I said, well, I'm going to tell you, I don't have pretension to be, you know, a great deep scholar of the topic.
sentences.zh: 所以，我说，好吧，我要告诉你，我并没有自称是什么了不起的该领域的深厚学者。

sentences.en: I would say rather I'm a really, really interested amateur.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我更像是一个真正、真正感兴趣的业余爱好者。

sentences.en: I'm a really very emotionally engaged reader of mythology.
sentences.zh: 我是一个对神话有着极高情感投入的读者。

sentences.en: And one of the people I talked to actually was a chair of religions at a university said to me, yeah, but you know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的人之一，实际上是一位大学的宗教系主任，他对我说，是的，但你知道自己在说什么。

sentences.en: And I thought that was pretty funny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: That kind of made my day.
sentences.zh: 这让我一整天心情都很好。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that was my trajectory.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我的轨迹。

sentences.en: My trajectory wasn't the usual.
sentences.zh: 我的轨迹并不寻常。

sentences.en: And as far as psychology goes, I don't think you can study mythology without bumping against psychology every step of the way.
sentences.zh: 就心理学而言，我认为你不可能在研究神话的同时，每一步都不与心理学发生碰撞。

sentences.en: I think in the sense of meaning, I, I'm, you know, you hear me say it over and over again,
sentences.zh: 我认为在意义感方面，我，我，你知道的，你听到我反复这么说，

sentences.en: but I think that so much is important about human beings having a sense of meaning and navigating their way through life.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对人类来说，拥有意义感以及驾驭生活是非常重要的。

sentences.en: I think that's the issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是关键所在。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of the things that used to give us a sense of meaning and hope are going away in the world, you know, even the younger generations, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为世界上许多过去能给我们带来意义感和希望的事物正在消失，你知道的，甚至年轻一代，你知道，

sentences.en: there's polls and they don't even think the planet will be around for their kids in the same capacity that it is now.
sentences.zh: 有民意调查显示，他们甚至认为这个地球将来无法像现在这样为他们的孩子存在了。

sentences.en: Or the economic system will allow them to have any, their kids to have any kind of semblance of life like we have.
sentences.zh: 或者经济体制不会允许他们的孩子拥有任何类似于我们现在这种生活的东西。

sentences.en: And not saying that's true or false, you know, but that that's a belief, you know, that people who grew up with an iPhone, you know, think before they're, you know, 13,
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是真是假，你知道，但这是一种信念，你知道的，那些和iPhone一起长大的人，你知道，在他们，你知道，13岁之前，

sentences.en: they are already sitting with this pretty dark existential stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们就已经在思考这些相当黑暗的存在主义问题了。

sentences.en: And when you see that in therapy, it's like the generational difference used to be 10 years apart.
sentences.zh: 当你在治疗中看到这一点时，就好像以前的代沟是相隔10年。

sentences.en: Now it's like when I see somebody 25 and somebody 19, the difference is vast, you know, the way that they see the world.
sentences.zh: 现在当我看到一个25岁的人和一个19岁的人时，差异是巨大的，你知道，他们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: Well, and I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: And I also find fascinating all this, you know, the fascination with apocalyptic stuff like zombie stuff and all that.
sentences.zh: 而且我也觉得所有这些，你知道的，对末日题材的痴迷，比如僵尸题材等等，都非常迷人。

sentences.en: And, you know, and I've had conversations, very intelligent, rational people said, you know, zombie apocalypse is strange and probably is very obviously fiction.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我曾与非常聪明、理性的人交谈过，他们说，你知道，僵尸末日很奇怪，而且很可能显然是虚构的。

sentences.en: But that type of apocalyptic thing is not so crazy.
sentences.zh: 但那种末日题材并不是那么疯狂。

sentences.en: And they really think that.
sentences.zh: 他们真的是这么想的。

sentences.en: And then when COVID came out, I remember a number of people's younger people, especially saying, well, you know, this is life imitating art.
sentences.zh: 然后当新冠疫情爆发时，我记得许多人——尤其是年轻人——说，嗯，你知道，这是生活在模仿艺术。

sentences.en: We've had all these movies, like outbreak and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们看过所有这些电影，比如《极度恐慌》以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And, and here we are with this.
sentences.zh: 而，而我们现在就身处其中。

sentences.en: And, you know, is there going that whole year was like, you know, political catastrophe and plague and fires and food famine.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那整整一年就像是，你知道的，政治灾难、瘟疫、火灾和粮食饥荒。

sentences.en: And like, it's just like the biblical.
sentences.zh: 就像《圣经》里的一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That was my comment always when, when did locusts show up, you know, but yeah, but I mean, but you talked, I'm still an optimist, but I'm old, you know, but I also think that,
sentences.zh: 每当蝗虫出现时，我总是这么评论，你知道的，但是，是的，我的意思是，但是你谈到——我仍然是个乐观主义者，但我老了，你知道，但我也认为，

sentences.en: you know, one thing when you get old is you, you've survived so many train wrecks that you say, I wouldn't worry about this too much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你老了的一个特点就是，你经历了那么多的列车相撞事故，你会说，我不用太担心这个。

sentences.en: But, uh, well, I think it's a combination of things are probably not sustainable.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，我认为这是多种因素的结合，可能无法持续。

sentences.en: There is going to be a change at some point.
sentences.zh: 在某个时间点将会发生改变。

sentences.en: And kids just have access to information where they were able to ask that question at six to Google.
sentences.zh: 孩子们只是拥有获取信息的渠道，他们在六岁时就能向谷歌提出这个问题。

sentences.en: Whereas most people get to college and they're like, whoa, whoa, what if nothing means anything?
sentences.zh: 而大多数人直到上大学时才会觉得，哇，哇，如果一切都没有意义怎么办？

sentences.en: You know, that's the first time they encounter each year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是他们第一次遇到这种事。

sentences.en: Anything is, you know, in their twenties.
sentences.zh: 任何事情都是，你知道的，在他们二十多岁的时候。

sentences.en: And now kids are sitting with that stuff at five, which is deprived of the pleasure of ignorance that others have enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 而现在孩子们在五岁时就已经在思考这些事情了，这剥夺了其他人曾经享受过的无知的快乐。

sentences.en: And I, as to say, when you talk to a seven year old, it sounds like Schopenhauer.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，当你和七岁的小孩交谈时，听起来就像叔本华一样。

sentences.en: That's very, very slippery.
sentences.zh: 那真是非常、非常微妙。

sentences.zh: 那么，你，你，你有没有，嗯，研究过荣格或做过任何荣格心理学，还是你只是对神话感兴趣？

sentences.en: All of the above, actually.
sentences.zh: 以上皆是，其实。

sentences.en: All of the above.
sentences.zh: 以上皆是。
