sentences.zh: 博览群书先生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, also the other thing too is, uh, I actually had a group of friends who, uh, that are Jungian reading group.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有一件事是，呃，我其实有一群朋友，呃，那是一个荣格读书小组。

sentences.en: And this is almost 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是将近40年前的事了。

sentences.en: And that was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And I read German.
sentences.zh: 而且我懂德语。

sentences.en: So I was another reason to read Jung.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我读荣格的另一个原因。

sentences.en: And, and unlike Freud, Jung is readable in German.
sentences.zh: 而且，与弗洛伊德不同，荣格的德语是可读的。

sentences.en: Uh, Freud, Freud hurts my brain when I read, try reading him in German, but Jung, I can get through pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 呃，弗洛伊德，我读弗洛伊德时脑子疼，试着用德语读他看看，但荣格的书我可以相当轻松地读完。

sentences.en: And, and, and it's interesting because I like when he discusses his trips, like his trips among the American Indians and describes, uh, his experiences with them and so forth.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，这很有趣，因为我喜欢他讨论自己的旅行，比如他在美洲印第安人中的旅行，并描述，呃，他与他们在一起的经历等等。

sentences.en: And how their mythology informs their sense of meaning and how they navigate through life.
sentences.zh: 以及他们的神话如何为他们的意义感提供信息，以及他们如何驾驭生活。

sentences.en: And, and I think that that's something that I'm still obsessed with.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为这依然是我所痴迷的东西。

sentences.en: Uh, and, uh, my poetry, you know, reflects that as well.
sentences.zh: 呃，而且，我的诗歌，你知道，也反映了这一点。

sentences.en: But, uh, I've always feel like life is hard enough, you know?
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，我一直觉得生活已经够艰难了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I'm sure you feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我确信你也有同感。

sentences.en: If you can somehow help people navigate through life, you're making your own life meaningful.
sentences.zh: 如果你能以某种方式帮助人们驾驭生活，你就是在让自己的生活变得有意义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I love the job that I have now, just being able to sit with patients.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我很喜欢我现在的工作，能坐下来陪陪患者。

sentences.en: I don't like the, the business part is kind of a means to an end just to make sure other people can work and we can build a clinic.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢商业化那部分，那只是一种手段，为了确保别人能工作，我们能建起诊所。

sentences.en: But I don't live for that.
sentences.zh: 但我不是为了那个而活。

sentences.en: I live for just sitting in a room with people and, um, helping them make meaning even when you can't make meaning.
sentences.zh: 我活着就是为了和人们坐在一个房间里，呃，帮他们寻找意义，哪怕在你觉得无法找到意义的时候。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And work always interrupted my gardening and poetry writing.
sentences.zh: 而且工作总是打扰我的园艺和写诗。

sentences.en: It's just a shame.
sentences.zh: 真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: And winemaking.
sentences.zh: 还有酿酒。

sentences.en: I was not interrupted, you know?
sentences.zh: 我可没被打扰，你知道吗？

sentences.en: You make wine?
sentences.zh: 你还会酿酒？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: And, uh, I gotta do that.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我得做那个。

sentences.en: That's good for your, you got, we live in Texas and we have grapes.
sentences.zh: 那对你的，你懂的，我们住在得克萨斯州，我们有葡萄。

sentences.en: I mean, what's wrong with, you know, it's all good stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有什么不好的，你知道的，这些都是好东西。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, it's, but it is, I've always felt, uh, most useful thing we can do is help other people navigate through life.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我是说，它确实是，我一直觉得，呃，我们能做的最有用的事就是帮助其他人度过人生。

sentences.en: And so I guess the way I would put it in, and mythology is, is built to help people navigate through life.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我的表达方式是，神话就是为了帮助人们度过人生而建立的。

sentences.en: I mean, my second.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的第二本。

sentences.en: It's an attempt to make meaning, you know?
sentences.zh: 这是一种寻找意义的尝试，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: My second book, Living Myths, like each stage of your life has, has a myth that has got a myth of some culture or many cultures that help you to navigate that phase of your life.
sentences.zh: 我的第二本书，《生活的神话》，就像你人生的每个阶段，都有一个神话，某种文化或多种文化的神话，来帮助你度过人生的那个阶段。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: Well, and I think, I know you've read them, um, but just for the listeners, in case anyone's not familiar, the Iliad of Mercea did, uh, Sacred and the Prophet,
sentences.zh: 好吧，而且我想，我知道你读过它们，嗯，但为了听众，以防有人不熟悉，米尔恰·伊利亚德写了，呃，《神圣与世俗》

sentences.en: which is a pretty early book about, um, study of religion and mythology.
sentences.zh: 那是一本关于，呃，宗教和神话研究的早期著作。

sentences.en: One of the things he did was, uh, you know, he would find these aboriginal tribes that had a stick and the whole history of the tribe is written on the stick.
sentences.zh: 他做的事情之一就是，你知道，他会找到那些有一根棍子的土著部落，部落的整个历史都写在那根棍子上。

sentences.en: And then the stick is the, the tent pole of your tent.
sentences.zh: 然后这根棍子就是你们帐篷的帐篷杆。

sentences.en: And then in the morning it falls in a direction and then you go where the stick tells you to go.
sentences.zh: 接着早晨它朝某个方向倒下，然后你就去棍子指引你去的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the great world axis, that's what it's so well.
sentences.zh: 还有伟大的世界轴心，这就是它的厉害之处。

sentences.en: So that's what was making their meaning, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他们在创造意义的方式，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And if the stick pointed to a river, oh, great, the stick wanted us to have water.
sentences.zh: 如果棍子指向一条河，哦，太好了，棍子想让我们有水。

sentences.en: Thank you, stick.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，棍子。

sentences.en: If it goes to a mountain, oh, it's a holy mountain.
sentences.zh: 如果它指向一座山，哦，这是一座神圣的山。

sentences.en: Thank you, stick.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，棍子。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: And he would talk to the tribes where the stick would have been lost in a flood or stolen by an enemy or something.
sentences.zh: 他会跟那些棍子在洪水中丢失或被敌人偷走的部落交谈。

sentences.en: And the people would just wander and die.
sentences.zh: 然后人们就会四处流浪，走向死亡。

sentences.en: Like they had no ability to make meaning out of, without the sticks.
sentences.zh: 就像他们没有棍子就无法创造意义一样。

sentences.en: And how many, and how many people do we encounter, right?
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了多少，究竟遇到了多少人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: It's we've, we've lost our stick or we're fighting about which stick the sticks say to go different directions.
sentences.zh: 就是我们，我们弄丢了我们的棍子，或者我们在争论棍子到底在说去不同的方向。

sentences.en: But, I mean, that's the primal myth is it's just, this is order and this is chaos.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，最初的神话就是，这就是秩序，这就是混乱。

sentences.en: And somebody goes from order into chaos and then turns the chaos into order.
sentences.zh: 有人从秩序走向混乱，然后把混乱转化为秩序。

sentences.en: You know, that's the primal myth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是最初的神话。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can get into all the archetypes that make that process more complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你可以研究所有让这个过程变得更复杂的原型。

sentences.en: But that's all it is.
sentences.zh: 但这就是它的全部。

sentences.en: It's what psychology is.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学。

sentences.en: It's what religion is.
sentences.zh: 这就是宗教。

sentences.en: And it's what myth is.
sentences.zh: 这也是神话。

sentences.en: Well, I look at, and look at Hindu mythology too, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我看看，再看看印度神话，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, you know, things are going to be created.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，事物将会被创造。

sentences.en: They're going to decay and they're going to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它们会衰败，然后被毁灭。

sentences.en: You can't get around it.
sentences.zh: 这是绕不开的。

sentences.en: But it'll happen again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 但这一切会一次又一次地发生。

sentences.en: And I always tell people, I say, you know, is that's a very pessimistic worldview.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉人们，我说，你知道，这是一种非常悲观的世界观。

sentences.en: I say, is it really?
sentences.zh: 我说，真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 其实不然。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不悲观。

sentences.en: It's a realistic point of view that, you know, I've been reading.
sentences.zh: 这是一种现实的观点，你知道的，我一直在读。

sentences.en: And that everything is a dream.
sentences.zh: 而且一切皆是梦。

sentences.en: That the, you know, Vishnu is dreaming everything into existence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，毗湿奴正把一切都梦进现实中。

sentences.en: But eventually, when Christian wakes up, he'll just be gone.
sentences.zh: 但最终，当克利须那醒来时，他就会直接消失。

sentences.en: We're just, we're juSt.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，我们只是。

sentences.en: Well, you know the Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道中国哲学家庄子吗？

sentences.en: Uh-uh.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm just, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: I didn't mean to interrupt you.
sentences.zh: 我不是故意打断你的。

sentences.en: No, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 没事，你继续。

sentences.en: I just, like, stimulated the Zhuangzi story.
sentences.zh: 我只是，突然想到了庄子的故事。

sentences.en: Zhuangzi had this thing called Zhuangzi's butterfly.
sentences.zh: 庄子有个东西叫庄周梦蝶。

sentences.en: And Martin Heidegger thought this was the coolest thing ever.
sentences.zh: 马丁·海德格尔觉得这是有史以来最酷的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: He thought this was very exciting.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And which Zhuangzi said, I woke up from a dream where I was a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 庄子说，我从一个梦中醒来，梦见自己是一只蝴蝶。

sentences.en: And I was, you know, flitting about from flower to flower and getting nectar and all this happy stuff.
sentences.zh: 我当时，你知道，在花丛中翩翩起舞，采食花蜜，还有诸如此类快乐的事情。

sentences.en: And then I woke up and I was Zhuangzi again.
sentences.zh: 然后我醒了，我又成了庄子。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, am I a butterfly that dreams about Zhuangzi?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我是梦见庄子的蝴蝶呢？

sentences.en: Or am I Zhuangzi who dreams about being a butterfly?
sentences.zh: 还是梦见自己是蝴蝶的庄子呢？

sentences.en: And I just love that story.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个故事了。

sentences.en: And then he said, yeah, he said, you know, it was fun being a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，对，他说，你知道，当蝴蝶挺好玩的。

sentences.en: You know, and I just like the way he said that, though.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我就是喜欢他那种说法。

sentences.en: It's like, you know.
sentences.zh: 就好像，你知道的。

sentences.en: And Martin Heidegger thought that was a great story.
sentences.zh: 马丁·海德格尔认为那是个很棒的故事。

sentences.en: He was a big fan of that story.
sentences.zh: 他是那个故事的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: It's probably challenging to some of Heidegger's stuff, too, because he was all that language is the house of being.
sentences.zh: 这可能也对海德格尔的一些观点构成了挑战，因为他主张语言是存在的居所。

sentences.en: And, you know, you're trapped with incognition.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你被困在认知之中。

sentences.en: And so if you're a butterfly and you don't have language and you still exist, what are you, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一只蝴蝶，你没有语言，但你仍然存在，你算什么呢，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Sein und sein.
sentences.zh: 存在与存在。

sentences.en: Und da sein.
sentences.zh: 还有此在。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was a happy guy.
sentences.zh: 对，他是个快乐的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's been a long time since my Heidegger classes at Swanee.
sentences.zh: 是的，自我当年在休瓦尼上海德格尔的课已经过去很久了。

sentences.en: Being in time is not a fun read in English.
sentences.zh: 英文版的《存在与时间》读起来可真没意思。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Und sein.
sentences.zh: 存在与存在。

sentences.en: Und sein.
sentences.zh: 还有存在。

sentences.en: Anyway, it just sounds so awful in German.
sentences.zh: 总之，用德语听起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But anyway, actually, I'm a great fan, though, of Carl Jaspersenegger.
sentences.zh: 不过不管怎样，实际上，我也非常崇拜卡尔·雅斯贝尔斯。

sentences.en: I guess he was a great fan of myth.
sentences.zh: 我想他也是神话的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: And he was the man who came up with the idea of the Axial Age.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个提出“轴心时代”概念的人。

sentences.en: All these religious, great religious thinkers emerged around the world somewhat simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 所有这些伟大的宗教思想家几乎同时在世界各地涌现。

sentences.en: And, you know, some, I think, did inform each other and some did not.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为有些确实互相启发了，有些则没有。

sentences.en: But he's a great one for saying, you know, he never took a Jungian pact.
sentences.zh: 但他非常棒的一点在于，你知道，他从未接受过荣格派。

sentences.en: But he was a great one, though, for saying that, you know, it's all about meaning.
sentences.zh: 但他真的很棒，总是说，这一切都关于意义。

sentences.en: People have got, like you said about this, it's all about meaning.
sentences.zh: 人们必须，就像你刚才说的，这一切都关于意义。

sentences.en: Everything everybody wants to do is about finding meaning and navigating life.
sentences.zh: 每个人想做的一切都是为了寻找意义和度过人生。

sentences.en: And that you can tell people what to expect in life, but until they experience it, they don't know how to navigate it.
sentences.zh: 你可以告诉人们生活中会期望什么，但在他们亲身经历之前，他们并不知道该如何应对。

sentences.en: So, you know, our order-making, I mean, I think part of the contradiction of human nature is our order-making principle, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们建立秩序的原则，我是说，我认为人性矛盾的一部分在于我们建立秩序的原则，你知道，

sentences.en: our ego that is the organizing principle of the psyche is what stops us from making meaning.
sentences.zh: 我们作为心灵组织原则的自我，正是阻碍我们寻找意义的东西。

sentences.en: Because we cling to it too rigidly.
sentences.zh: 因为我们对它抓得太紧了。

sentences.en: And so we have to dissolve it and then go under the ego and under language even into the body and the emotional and the transcendental space.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须瓦解它，然后潜入自我之下，甚至越过语言，深入身体、情感和超越的空间。

sentences.en: And that is how we come back from the descent, you know, like Campbell says in The Hero's Journey or Jung says with The Shadow, to we come back with a greater meaning.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们从深渊中归来的方式，你知道的，就像坎伯在《英雄之旅》中所说，或者荣格在面对《阴影》时所说，我们带着更重大的意义归来。

sentences.en: But we can't quite take all of the information from that place with us, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法把那个地方的所有信息完全带回，你知道的。

sentences.en: Well, I was at Tillich too, like Tillich's view, that the whole process of life is finding the God behind God.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我也想到了蒂利希，就像蒂利希的观点，整个生命的过程就是寻找上帝背后的上帝。

sentences.en: In other words, what you think of as God is going to be shattered by what God is in reality to you in the next phase.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你在下一阶段所认为的上帝，将被上帝对你而言的真实面目所击碎。

sentences.en: And I always like that thought that Tillich had about that.
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢蒂利希关于这一点的想法。

sentences.en: Because it doesn't stop, that the reality of God continues to unfold as you know it and as you cry.
sentences.zh: 因为它不会停止，上帝的现实随着你的认知和呼喊不断展开。

sentences.en: Right, and it's the reality of self as well.
sentences.zh: 没错，这也是自我的现实。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's the problem with a lot of different models of psychology is that they're perfectly fine if you're here, you know.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为许多不同的心理学模型的问题在于，如果你正处于某个特定阶段，它们完全没问题，你知道的。

sentences.en: So if you're like coming out of recovery or if you're 21 and you broke up with your boyfriend for the first time in college or this, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你刚从戒瘾中恢复，或者你21岁，在大学里第一次和男朋友分手，或者诸如此类，你知道，

sentences.en: they're fine with helping you with that.
sentences.zh: 它们在帮应对这些方面没问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, 10, 20 years of cognitive behavioral therapy, you know, I can't imagine you'd be doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，进行10年、20年的认知行为疗法，你知道，我无法想象你会一直做同样的事情。

sentences.en: Like, what is it?
sentences.zh: 比如，那是什么？

sentences.en: Irvin Yalom is the existential psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 欧文·亚隆是存在主义心理学家。

sentences.en: Or the existential psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 或者说存在主义心理学家。

sentences.en: And he would always kind of put fun at the cognitive people that don't really do anything other than ego management strategies, which is fine, you know.
sentences.zh: 他总是喜欢取笑那些认知学派的人，他们除了自我管理策略之外什么也不做，虽然这也无可厚非，你知道的。

sentences.en: But it was always like, I mean, when CBT therapists get sick, why do they come see me?
sentences.zh: 但总是让人觉得，我是说，当CBT治疗师生病时，他们为什么来看我？

sentences.en: Why don't they go to another CBT therapist if it's so great?
sentences.zh: 既然它这么厉害，他们为什么不去找另一个CBT治疗师？

sentences.en: And it's a script, you know, you're, you're, if the client says this, then you say this is manualizable.
sentences.zh: 那是个剧本，你知道的，你，如果客户这么说，你就这么说，这是可以写成手册的。

sentences.en: And because it's manualizable, you already know how it works.
sentences.zh: 正因为它是可以写成手册的，你早就知道它是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: So there's no point in going to see one.
sentences.zh: 所以去看他们根本没有任何意义。

sentences.en: And then there's a lot of people to say they do CBT.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多人声称他们做的是CBT。

sentences.en: But then when you sit with them in therapy or you work with them, they're really doing more of an attachment existential thing.
sentences.zh: 但当你和他们在疗程中坐在一起或与他们共事时，他们实际上在做更多关于依恋和存在主义的事情。

sentences.en: You know, they've figured out, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们自己琢磨出来了。

sentences.en: Oh, physician, heal thyself.
sentences.zh: 哦，医者不能自医。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, that's great stuff.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, all these metaphors for mythology.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，所有这些神话的隐喻。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, I think that's one of the biggest things is it can kind of take part of psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为这是最大的事情之一，它可以借用一部分心理学。

sentences.en: The thing that is challenging is you've got to take people outside of their experience to make them kind of doubt their assumptions.
sentences.zh: 具有挑战性的事情是，你必须把人们带出他们的体验之外，让他们开始怀疑自己的假设。

sentences.en: But that is threatening.
sentences.zh: 但这让人感到受到威胁。

sentences.en: So you have to do that in a way that doesn't make somebody defensive.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须以一种不会引起对方防御的方式来做这件事。

sentences.en: And mythology is a great way to do that because you're taking somebody and you're being like, hey, this is what's going on with you.
sentences.zh: 而神话就是做到这一点的绝佳方法，因为你把一个人拉进来，然后说，嘿，这就是你身上发生的事。

sentences.en: But you're not saying that.
sentences.zh: 但你并不是直接这么说的。

sentences.en: You're being like, you know, there was this centaur, Chiron, and he could heal everybody.
sentences.zh: 你就像是在说，你知道，曾经有这样一个半人马，喀戎，他能治愈所有人。

sentences.en: But he had this wound that he couldn't heal.
sentences.zh: 但他有一个无法治愈的伤口。

sentences.en: But I think the reason that he could heal everyone is because he was in such pain.
sentences.zh: 但我想他能治愈所有人，原因正是他身处极大的痛苦之中。

sentences.en: And then the person's like, oh, holy shit, that's me.
sentences.zh: 然后那个人就会觉得，天哪，这正是我。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And Chiron was a centaur of attention.
sentences.zh: 凯戎是所有人关注的“半人马”。

sentences.en: He was a what?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: The centaur of attention.
sentences.zh: 关注的半人马。

sentences.en: Oh, what do you mean there?
sentences.zh: 哦，你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: The center of attention.
sentences.zh: 关注的中心。

sentences.en: I was trying to make it that fun.
sentences.zh: 我只是想让它变得那么有趣。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: You know, when you have to explain a joke, it's not that good a joke.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你不得不解释一个笑话时，这个笑话就没那么好了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: The audio kind of dipped for a minute.
sentences.zh: 音频刚刚好像有点模糊了。

sentences.en: I thought I was just missed.
sentences.zh: 我以为我只是没对准。

sentences.en: I thought the noise canceling was mushy.
sentences.zh: 我还以为降噪效果有点糊。

sentences.en: You know, what's really interesting is when I talk to young people, especially, and they're talking about Game of Thrones, I just kind of sit back and grin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，真正有趣的是，当我跟年轻人交谈时，尤其是当他们谈到《权力的游戏》时，我就只是坐着笑一笑。

sentences.en: Because, hey, I can give you Games of Thrones mythology from here till, you know, heck won't have it, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，嘿，从现在到天荒地老，我都能给你讲《权力的游戏》的神话背景，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's so much of, and I really, what Martin wrote in Game of Thrones is really brilliant, but it's all very mythologically based.
sentences.zh: 因为这里面有太多东西了。马丁在《权力的游戏》里写的东西真的非常精彩，但它们都有着深厚的神话基础。

sentences.en: And all of the themes and archetypes and even episodes are mythologically based.
sentences.zh: 所有的主题、原型甚至情节都基于神话。

sentences.en: And why does that resonate?
sentences.zh: 为什么这能引起共鸣？

sentences.en: Well, you and I know why it resonates.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你我都清楚为什么它能引起共鸣。

sentences.en: Because this is their own human journey.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是他们自己的心路历程。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're seeing things, seeing conflict and seeing issues that may be not play, obviously, in the warrior stance of their daily life,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们看到的种种事物、冲突和问题，可能并不明显展现在他们日常生活中的战士姿态里，

sentences.en: but they play in their daily life.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实在日常生活中发挥着作用。

sentences.en: All of those things, you know, betrayal and loyalty and victory and defeat and failure and success.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情，你知道，背叛与忠诚、胜利与失败、挫折与成功。

sentences.en: And ambition and not realizing that you're the bad guy.
sentences.zh: 还有雄心勃勃，却意识不到自己才是那个坏人。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Being identifying with your own victimhood and suffering that you don't realize that you're victimizing others, you know.
sentences.zh: 认同于自身的受害者心态与苦难，却意识不到自己其实在加害别人，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yes, and scuttling yourself, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且自毁前程，你知道。

sentences.en: And that's what I always think is really interesting is, you know, telling a person the most painful things you have to tell the other human being is, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直觉得非常有意思的地方，你知道，对一个人说出你不得不对另一个人说的最痛苦的话，你知道，

sentences.en: what you're doing is scuttling yourself.
sentences.zh: 你所做的事其实就是在自我拆台。

sentences.en: But it's true, and it's a great theme in mythology that, you know, the hero is just blindly rushing ahead and his vulnerability is obvious to all of us watching him,
sentences.zh: 但这是真的，神话中有一个很棒的主题，你知道，英雄只是盲目前冲，他的脆弱在我们这些旁观者看来显而易见，

sentences.en: but everyone but him.
sentences.zh: 除了他自己，所有人都看出来了。

sentences.en: And then you say, you know, that it speaks to the human tendency to be not introspective enough to see where you're going to scuttle yourself, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现，这反映了人性中普遍缺乏内省的倾向，看不到自己会在哪里自毁前程，你知道。

sentences.en: I think that was very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有意思。

sentences.en: Can you parse what you mean by scuttle there, for the listener?
sentences.zh: 你能为听众解释一下你刚才用的“自毁（scuttle）”是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，对不起。

sentences.en: Like you scuttle a shit.
sentences.zh: 就像你凿沉一艘船（scuttle a ship）。

sentences.en: Like you cause the sink.
sentences.zh: 就像你导致它下沉。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I'm used to that term.
sentences.zh: 我习惯用这个词了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Let's just make sure everyone can understand.
sentences.zh: 我们得确保每个人都能听懂。

sentences.en: I mean, we feel like the enemy is out here, but really the thing defeating us is inside.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们总觉得敌人在外面，但真正击败我们的其实是内心。

sentences.en: You trip yourself.
sentences.zh: 你总是自己绊倒自己。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You trip yourself.
sentences.zh: 你总是自己绊倒自己。

sentences.en: I don't want to use the word defeat yourself, because that's a little bit too final.
sentences.zh: 我不想用“打败你自己”这个词，因为那听起来有点太绝对了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But you trip yourself.
sentences.zh: 但你确实是自己绊倒了自己。

sentences.en: You, you, you, you set yourself back through choices you've made that you are not seeing the fact that those choices will set you back.
sentences.zh: 你，你，你，你由于自己做出的选择而让自己倒退，却没有意识到这些选择会拖累你。

sentences.en: Have you ever read Neil Gaiman?
sentences.zh: 你读过尼尔·盖曼的作品吗？

sentences.en: You ever read him?
sentences.zh: 你读过他的书吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，读过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I read a lot of Neil Gaiman in high school.
sentences.zh: 我上高中的时候读过很多尼尔·盖曼的书。

sentences.en: Behind me on the shelves, you will see much Neil Gaiman.
sentences.zh: 我身后的书架上，你就能看到很多尼尔·盖曼的作品。

sentences.en: I always felt like he was a more interesting thinker than a writer.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得他比起作家，更是一个有趣的思想者。

sentences.en: Like his writing is kind of in service of the idea, not the idea in service of the writing, which I like.
sentences.zh: 就像他的写作在某种程度上是为理念服务的，而不是理念为写作服务，我很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: I like stuff.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种东西。

sentences.en: I get really bored when it's like people will probably be up in arMs.
sentences.zh: 如果人们可能会为此群情激愤，我会觉得很无聊。

sentences.en: But like something like Lolita, like I just, I have a hard time going through because it's so well done,
sentences.zh: 但像《洛丽塔》这样的作品，我读起来觉得很吃力，因为虽然它写得非常好，

sentences.en: but it's just kind of this character thing and you're reinforcing the theme.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一种角色塑造，而且你在不断强化这个主题。

sentences.en: And like, I want super rich, you know, density of ideas and the things.
sentences.zh: 而我想要的是极其丰富、密度极高的思想和事物。

sentences.en: And Gaiman's not the best writer, at least he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 盖曼并不是最好的作家，至少以前不是。

sentences.en: With the American Gods era, he was kind of shifting from comics to that.
sentences.zh: 在《美国众神》那个时期，他正从漫画创作转向那种文风。

sentences.en: But Ocean at the End of the Lane, I really think is like a perfect book.
sentences.zh: 但我真的觉得《巷尾的童年》是一本完美的书。

sentences.en: It's like that's the book he was trying to write for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 感觉那就是他花了十年时间一直想要写出来的书。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so funny.
sentences.zh: 对，太有趣了。

sentences.en: I've always thought of him as a great narrator.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为他是个伟大的讲述者。

sentences.en: He was a narrative guy.
sentences.zh: 他是一个擅长叙事的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's a structured guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个讲究结构的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, a structured guy.
sentences.zh: 对，讲究结构的人。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: How would I put it?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么说呢？

sentences.en: Who would you rather have at the coffee pot, him or Vladimir Nabokov, the guy who wrote Lolita?
sentences.zh: 你会更愿意和谁一起喝咖啡，是他，还是写了《洛丽塔》的弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫？

sentences.en: I would take Gaiman any day because I think he's, how do I put it?
sentences.zh: 我随时都选盖曼，因为我觉得他，我该怎么说呢？

sentences.en: He's very astute.
sentences.zh: 他非常敏锐。

sentences.en: He is very attuned and intuitive to human beings that would make them tick.
sentences.zh: 他对人类及其心理机制有着极高的契合度和直觉。

sentences.en: And that's why I always liked him.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直喜欢他的原因。

sentences.en: I always liked Robert Graves for that reason because he was very good in saying, you know,
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢罗伯特·格雷夫斯，也是出于这个原因，因为他很擅长说，你看，

sentences.en: here's what had happened that myth.
sentences.zh: 这就是神话中发生的事情。

sentences.en: Now, hmm, what does that make you think about?
sentences.zh: 现在，嗯，这让你联想到了什么？

sentences.en: Hmm?
sentences.zh: 嗯？

sentences.en: Who does that remind you of?
sentences.zh: 这让你想起谁了？

sentences.en: He doesn't say it in so many words, but he leads you to that point like, well, now, what does that remind you of?
sentences.zh: 他没有明说，但他引导你走到这一步，心想，好吧，这让你想起什么了？

sentences.en: And I love that because it's like somebody said to me, why in the heck are you reading mythology?
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这样了，因为就像有人对我说，你到底为什么要读神话？

sentences.en: That stuff is dead.
sentences.zh: 那些东西早就过时了。

sentences.en: That stuff's old.
sentences.zh: 那些都是老古董了。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, here, let's open a myth.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，来吧，我们翻开一个神话。

sentences.en: Let's read it.
sentences.zh: 我们来读读它。

sentences.en: Who does that remind you of?
sentences.zh: 这让你想起谁了？

sentences.en: Does that ring a bell?
sentences.zh: 这难道不让你觉得耳熟吗？

sentences.en: And it always does.
sentences.zh: 而它总是能直击人心。

sentences.en: Well, in Ocean and the End of the Lane, kind of what you're talking about, that making order
sentences.zh: 嗯，在《巷尾的童年》里，就像你刚才谈到的那样，从混乱中建立秩序，

sentences.en: out of chaos and that all psychology is this descent to let go of what we think we are to become what we really are and accept change and all that.
sentences.zh: 所有的心理学其实都是这样一个下沉过程：放下我们自以为是的模样，去成为真正的自己，并接受改变等等。

sentences.en: And there's like a metaphor towards the end of that book where the narrator's talking about
sentences.zh: 在那本书的结尾附近有一个比喻，讲的是叙述者

sentences.en: going into the ocean and they're like, as they are dissolving in the ocean, they're like,
sentences.zh: 走入海洋，他们仿佛在海洋中消融，并说道：

sentences.en: I am able to understand how everything works.
sentences.zh: 我能够理解万物是如何运作的。

sentences.en: I'm able to see from all perspectives.
sentences.zh: 我能够从所有视角进行观察。

sentences.en: I'm able to understand.
sentences.zh: 我能够理解一切。

sentences.en: I see everything so clearly, but that can't fit into a person.
sentences.zh: 我把一切都看得如此清晰，但这无法装进一个凡人的躯壳里。

sentences.en: And if you stay there, you become nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果你留在那里，你将化为虚无。

sentences.en: You become everything, but you become nothing.
sentences.zh: 你将成为万物，但你也将一无所有。

sentences.en: You dissolve.
sentences.zh: 你会彻底消融。

sentences.en: And look at the Bhagavad Gita with Arjuna and Krishna's conversation.
sentences.zh: 再来看看《薄伽梵歌》中阿周那和克里希纳的对话。

sentences.en: And it's like, if you do what you think you're supposed to do, you're going to be doing exactly the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 这就好像，如果你去做你以为自己应该做的事，你就会大错特错。

sentences.en: And if you do what you're supposed to do, it's going to break your heart.
sentences.zh: 而如果你去做你真正该做的事，它又会让你心碎。

sentences.en: And I always thought that was just the most brilliant analysis of human life, right?
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得这是对人类生命最精彩的剖析，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, and in the Bhagavad Gita, that's one of my favorite lines is that, behold, I have become time, even without your sword, all these willyards which turn into dust and die.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在《薄伽梵歌》中，我最喜欢的一句台词是：看哪，我已化身时间，纵然没有你的宝剑，所有这些勇士也将化为尘土而消亡。

sentences.en: He's trying, the book, if anyone, it's a Hindu religious book, but Vishnu is trying to convince a prince to go into a battle and fight.
sentences.zh: 这本书，如果硬要说的话，是一部印度教宗教典籍，但其中毗湿奴正试图说服一位王子上战场去战斗。

sentences.en: And the prince is trying to navel gaze and not do it.
sentences.zh: 而这位王子却在一味沉思内省，迟迟不肯行动。

sentences.en: Well, he's also, I'm going to have to kill my relatives.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他还在想：我得亲手杀死我的亲人。

sentences.en: That's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's trying to avoid, you know, this complicated decision.
sentences.zh: 对，他试图逃避，你知道，这个复杂的决定。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, well, look, I've become time.
sentences.zh: 于是克里希纳说，你看，我已化身时间。

sentences.en: Even without your sword, all these people will turn to dust and die, even if you do nothing.
sentences.zh: 纵然你什么都不做，没有你的宝剑，所有人也终将化为尘土而消亡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the other thing I always like to, too, is Arjuna is the audience's perspective in the story.
sentences.zh: 还有一点我也很喜欢，那就是阿周那在故事中代表了观众的视角。

sentences.en: It's part of a greater thing called the Marabata, which is a Hindu epic.
sentences.zh: 它是印度教史诗《摩诃婆罗多》中宏大篇章的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's the segment of where Arjuna, the charioteer, is about to go into battle against his cousins.
sentences.zh: 这一段讲的是作为御者的阿周那即将与他的表亲们开战。

sentences.en: And it's the epic battle of good and evil.
sentences.zh: 这是一场正义与邪恶的史诗之战。

sentences.en: But some are good and some are evil and some are a little bit more good than evil.
sentences.zh: 但其中有些人是好的，有些人是邪恶的，还有些人则是亦正亦邪、善多于恶。

sentences.en: And there's a little bit more going on there.
sentences.zh: 情况要远比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: And Krishna shows up and says, you know, you've got to do something.
sentences.zh: 然后克里希纳出现并说道，你知道，你必须做点什么。

sentences.en: This is your duty.
sentences.zh: 这是你的职责。

sentences.en: OK, you are.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是你。

sentences.en: This is your dharma.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的天职（法）。

sentences.en: This is what you were made to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你生来就要做的事。

sentences.en: And the guy's like, yeah, I don't want to do this.
sentences.zh: 而那个人却说，好吧，我不想这么做。

sentences.en: Here are the reasons why.
sentences.zh: 原因如下。

sentences.en: It's a great discussion because every human being goes through that.
sentences.zh: 这是一场极佳的探讨，因为每个人都会经历这种阶段。

sentences.en: Well, it's not really about war or not war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实无关乎战争与否。

sentences.en: It's about the way that we make decisions and make meaning.
sentences.zh: 它关乎我们如何做出决策并赋予意义。

sentences.en: I mean, so many of the people who are citing the Bhagavad Gita, like Gandhi, they're citing it as a work of arguing for peace and arguing for nonviolence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，许多引用《薄伽梵歌》的人，比如甘地，都是把它当作一部主张和平与非暴力的作品来引用的。

sentences.en: But the whole text is a debate about a guy needs to go fight a war against his family.
sentences.zh: 但整部文本实际上是一场关于一个人需要与自己的家族开战的辩论。

sentences.en: But the context is what leads to the point you just made, which is in regards to who wins this war, you're all going to be gone.
sentences.zh: 然而其语境最终引出了你刚才提到的观点，那就是无论谁赢得这场战争，你们终将全部消逝。

sentences.en: Victory is your victory is not that it's not that big a deal.
sentences.zh: 胜利，你的胜利其实没那么了不起。

sentences.en: So and there are no winners in time.
sentences.zh: 所以在时间面前，没有真正的赢家。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And it's this is how it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是如此。

sentences.en: And I love reading a Bhagavad Gita.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢阅读《薄伽梵歌》。

sentences.en: I read it many, many, many times.
sentences.zh: 我读过很多很多遍。

sentences.en: In fact, on my bedstead, I've got a Bible and I have Gandhi's translation of the Bhagavad
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我的床头，放着一本圣经和一本甘地翻译的《薄伽梵歌》，

sentences.en: Gita because he always has little commentaries in there in the margins.
sentences.zh: 因为他在页边空白处写了很多简短的评论。

sentences.en: So, well, here's what I think was in Arjuna's mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，以下是我认为当时阿周那心中的想法。

sentences.en: Here's what Krishna was trying to tell him.
sentences.zh: 这就是克里希纳当时试图告诉他的道理。

sentences.en: It was written.
sentences.zh: 这是写下来的。

sentences.en: And his translation was written for businessmen and people who really didn't, weren't Sanskrit scholars, but needed to read the Bhagavad Gita, he thought.
sentences.zh: 他认为，他的翻译是为商界人士以及并非梵文学者、但又需要阅读《薄伽梵歌》的人写的。

sentences.en: So it's my favorite version that I have.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我最喜欢的一个版本。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think we've kind of answered the question about why mythology is important to study and why it's a part of psychology.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，我想我们已经回答了关于为什么研究神话很重要以及为什么它是心理学一部分的问题。

sentences.en: What about poetry?
sentences.zh: 那诗歌呢？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the other half of the stuff that you do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是你所做事情的另一半。

sentences.en: You're a poet now.
sentences.zh: 你现在是个诗人了。

sentences.en: You've got a blog about poetry.
sentences.zh: 你有一个关于诗歌的博客。

sentences.en: Do you publish poems on print or do you just do them on the web?
sentences.zh: 你在纸质媒体上发表诗歌，还是只在网络上发表？

sentences.en: I'm doing on the blog now and I'm in the process of doing some in print.
sentences.zh: 我现在在博客上发表，而且也正在筹备一些纸质出版物。

sentences.en: I'm also in the process of translating my poetry to Turkish, which is, that's my little intellectual exercise to keep me, keep my old brain cells working.
sentences.zh: 我也正在把我的诗歌翻译成土耳其语，这是我的一个小小的智力练习，好让我的老脑细胞保持运转。

sentences.en: But I've had a really good response to the website and encourage people, of course, to look at it and also make comments.
sentences.zh: 不过我的网站反响很好，当然，我也鼓励大家去看看并留下评论。

sentences.en: We'll link to it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目介绍里放上链接。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the things I put in there, by the way, is the critics were somewhat right, is what I say, because I address the issue of criticism and how when you are doing
sentences.zh: 而且，顺便说一句，我在里面提到的一点是，批评家们在某种程度上是对的，我是这么说的，因为我探讨了批评这个话题，以及当你...

sentences.en: anything like writing or painting or thinking that there's criticism and how do you take constructive criticism?
sentences.zh: 在做写作、绘画或思考之类的任何事情时，都会面临批评，你该如何接受建设性的批评？

sentences.en: And in retrospect, you realize that a lot of the criticism, whatever the person's motive
sentences.zh: 回过头来看，你会发现很多批评，不管对方的动机是什么...

sentences.en: is useful, is very useful and helps you to think.
sentences.zh: 都是有用的，非常有用，能帮你进行思考。

sentences.en: And you can say, yeah, well, his or her, you know, motive was terrible.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，好吧，他或她的动机确实太糟了。

sentences.en: They were just, this isn't like, okay, but maybe they said something you may want to consider.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在……这倒不是说……好吧，但也许他们说了一些你可能需要考虑的话。

sentences.en: And that was one topic I've done.
sentences.zh: 这是我做过的一个主题。

sentences.en: But I try to do things that I think, I listen to people, and I try to do things that help them navigate, right?
sentences.zh: 但我尽量去做那些我认为……我倾听人们的心声，并尽量做那些能帮助他们找到方向的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: And someone informed by mythology, someone informed by introspection and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 一个受神话启迪的人，一个受内省和哲学启迪的人。

sentences.en: And a couple of the poems that are really popular, I mean, if I may, I'll read them for you.
sentences.zh: 有几首非常受欢迎的诗，如果可以的话，我读给你们听听。

sentences.en: That would be wonderful.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: I'd love for you to read some.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意听你读几首。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: Well, the one that is most popular and written is Unselfing.
sentences.zh: 最受欢迎且已经写好的那一首叫做《去自我化》（Unselfing）。

sentences.en: And there's a prologue to it, where Terand Russell uses the term unselfing to describe the practice of going outside yourself, your needs, and your present situation to connect
sentences.zh: 它有一个前言，特伦特·罗素用“去自我化”这个词来描述这样一种实践：超越自我、超越你的需求和当前的处境，去与...

sentences.en: with others and with things greater than oneself.
sentences.zh: 他人以及比自我更伟大的事物建立连接。

sentences.en: Hmm, I should say yourself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我应该说“超越你自己”。

sentences.en: I realize an inconsistency there.
sentences.zh: 我意识到那里有点不一致。

sentences.en: In Russell's case, the wonders of science, mathematics, and the universe.
sentences.zh: 在罗素的例子中，那是科学、数学和宇宙的奇迹。

sentences.en: This led to a meditation on unselfing.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场关于“去自我化”的沉思。

sentences.en: For Christians, it seems particularly appropriate during Lent, which is now.
sentences.zh: 对基督徒来说，在大斋期（也就是现在）期间，这显得尤为应景。

sentences.en: Now, I also think it's very fitting for Ramadan, or for Muslims at Ramadan.
sentences.zh: 同时，我也认为这非常适合斋月，适合穆斯林在斋月期间阅读。

sentences.en: So I'll read it for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我读给你们听听。

sentences.en: Myself is me.
sentences.zh: “自我”就是我自己。

sentences.en: Imagine myself as a hot air balloon with many heavy rocks attached to it by ropes, anchoring it firmly to the ground.
sentences.zh: 把自己想象成一个热气球，许多沉重的石头用绳子拴在它上面，将其牢牢地锚定在地面上。

sentences.en: The balloon is my spirit, and the rocks are my own concerns, needs, wishes, worries, desires,
sentences.zh: 气球是我的精神，而这些石头是我自己的关切、需求、愿望、担忧、欲望...

sentences.en: preoccupied, preoccupations, preconceived notions, prejudices, fears, and worries about things that will never happen.
sentences.zh: 执念、成见、偏见、恐惧，以及对永远不会发生的事情的忧虑。

sentences.en: If I am in this balloon and look down, that is all I see.
sentences.zh: 如果我在这个气球里向下看，我看到的就只有这些。

sentences.en: I look up, however, I see the infinite sky, and I know that if I cut the ropes to these rocks weighing me down, the balloon will soar, and I will see new panoramas.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我向上看，我就会看到无限的天空，并且我知道，如果我割断拴着这些累赘石头的绳子，气球就会翱翔，我将看到新的全景。

sentences.en: I will see others.
sentences.zh: 我将看到他人。

sentences.en: I will see the place I had been from a loftier height, and see just how small it is.
sentences.zh: 我将从一个更高的视角看到我曾经所在的地方，并发现它是多么渺小。

sentences.en: Unself, cut the ropes to your own petty concerns and soar.
sentences.zh: 去自我化吧，割断拴住你那些琐碎担忧的绳子，去翱翔吧。

sentences.en: Move higher towards visions beyond myself, toward things greater than the self where I am.
sentences.zh: 向着超越自我的愿景移动，向着比我所在的自我更伟大的事物前进。

sentences.en: My spirit will rise beyond the self that weighs me down, and as I rise and soar, what was once large becomes small.
sentences.zh: 我的精神将超越那个拖累我的自我，随着我上升和翱翔，曾经巨大的东西变得渺小。

sentences.en: My heart expands beyond me to embrace others, and what was small in my spirit becomes greater as it rises.
sentences.zh: 我的心超越了自我去拥抱他人，而我精神中原本渺小的部分在上升时变得更加伟大。

sentences.en: That was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那太美了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: That was fun.
sentences.zh: 那很有趣。

sentences.en: I enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我很享受。

sentences.en: I do my writing of poeMs.
sentences.zh: 我写诗。

sentences.en: I'm going to tell you, this is kind of fun.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你们，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: Early, early in the morning, when I first get up, I think, I ponder, I meditate, I read things, and I make little notes, right?
sentences.zh: 清晨，一大清早，当我刚起床时，我会思考、默想、沉思、阅读各种东西，然后做点小笔记，对吧？

sentences.en: And I do that one day, and the poem usually gets written a day or two later, because I then end up arguing with myself, saying, that's not what you're going to say.
sentences.zh: 我有一天会这样做，诗通常会在一两天后写出来，因为我最后会跟自己争论，说，这不是你要说的话。

sentences.en: That's kind of stupid, or that's, I really, that sounds awfully, you know, Vaseline on the lens, Hallmark-y, so don't do that.
sentences.zh: 这有点蠢，或者说，我真的觉得这听起来太像……你知道的，就像镜头上抹了凡士林、 Hallmark贺卡那种调调，所以别这么写。

sentences.en: And so that's how these things come out.
sentences.zh: 这就是这些作品诞生的过程。

sentences.en: Another one I'm going to read is one of my most popular ones.
sentences.zh: 我要读的另一首是我最受欢迎的诗作之一。

sentences.en: I've seen getting good feedback, and it's called, What Does It Matter to Me?
sentences.zh: 我看到它获得了很好的反馈，它叫做《这与我何干？》（What Does It Matter to Me?）。

sentences.en: And I'm going to warn you up front, it's very straightforward, not a lot of metaphor to work through or anything.
sentences.zh: 我先向你们预告一下，这首诗非常直白，没有什么需要琢磨的隐喻之类的东西。

sentences.en: It starts with a quote, if you feel pain, you are alive.
sentences.zh: 它以一句名言开头：“如果你感到疼痛，你还活着。如果你感受到他人的疼痛，你才是一个人类”但他们会为此干杯的。

sentences.en: If you feel another's pain, you're a human, but they'll toast on it.
What does, and guess what this is inspired by, by the way, let you hear the whole poem go, oh yeah, I get it.
sentences.zh: 你们猜猜这受了什么启发，顺便说一句，等你们听完整首诗就会说，哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: What does it matter to me when there's a war on the other side of the earth?
sentences.zh: 当地球另一端发生战争时，这与我何干？

sentences.en: Very sad.
sentences.zh: 非常悲伤。

sentences.en: Quite tragic.
sentences.zh: 相当悲惨。

sentences.en: Sorry to hear about that.
sentences.zh: 听到这消息很难过。

sentences.en: But it isn't my war.
sentences.zh: 但这不是我的战争。

sentences.en: What does it matter when there's an earthquake on the other side of the earth that kills as many people as live in most small towns?
sentences.zh: 当地球另一端发生了一场地震，夺去了相当于大多数小镇人口的生命时，这又与我何干？

sentences.en: Tragic.
sentences.zh: 真惨。

sentences.en: I feel sorry for that.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到难过。

sentences.en: What a shame.
sentences.zh: 太遗憾了。

sentences.en: Should I buy a hot tub?
sentences.zh: 我是不是该买个按摩浴缸？

sentences.en: Look, we really should install track lighting in the dining room.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们真的应该在餐厅里安装轨道灯。

sentences.en: Why does, what does it matter that a child is hungry in the other end of the earth?
sentences.zh: 为什么……地球另一端的一个孩子在挨饿，这与我何干？

sentences.en: After all, people shouldn't have so many children.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，人们不应该生那么多孩子。

sentences.en: Well, it matters, I suppose, really, but they always have problems there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这确实有关系，但他们那里总是状况不断。

sentences.en: If it's on the other side of the world, I really can't see it.
sentences.zh: 如果它发生在世界的另一端，我根本看不见。

sentences.en: So it doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它不存在。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这无关紧要。

sentences.en: Or does it matter?
sentences.zh: 或者说这真的无关紧要吗？

sentences.en: It isn't my problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的问题。

sentences.en: If it appears on the screen, I can change the channel and relax by watching a zombie apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 如果它出现在屏幕上，我可以换个频道，看丧尸末日来放松一下。

sentences.en: The human condition is so tragic, but it's not my condition.
sentences.zh: 人类的境况是如此悲惨，但这不是我的境况。

sentences.en: Well, perhaps that's the real tragedy because they are humans and then there is me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许这才是真正的悲剧，因为他们是人，而我是我。

sentences.en: My indifference means that I'm not human, but some other kind of creature.
sentences.zh: 我的冷漠意味着我不是人类，而是某种别的生物。

sentences.en: But if I see the things I'd rather not see, it will make me human.
sentences.zh: 但如果我去看那些我宁愿不看的东西，它就会让我成为真正的人。

sentences.en: And then those things will matter to me.
sentences.zh: 然后，这些事情对我就有了意义。

sentences.en: The empty stomach of a child will become the emptiness in my heart.
sentences.zh: 孩子空空如也的肚子将变成我心中的空虚。

sentences.en: The empty hand of another will matter when it touches my hand.
sentences.zh: 当他人的手触碰我的手时，这只空着的手便有了意义。

sentences.en: And fullness of soul is when other souls matter.
sentences.zh: 灵魂的丰盈在于其他灵魂对你而言是有意义的。

sentences.en: Beauty of face is not an expensive cream, but in seeing the beauty of another human face in our eyes.
sentences.zh: 面容的美丽不在于昂贵的面霜，而在于从我们眼中看到另一张人类面孔的美丽。

sentences.en: And the best defense against aging is a maturity that is so young that it sees itself in a hungry child.
sentences.zh: 而对抗衰老的最佳防御，是一种如此年轻的成熟，它能在饥饿的孩子身上看到自己的倒影。

sentences.en: And you both matter a little more.
sentences.zh: 你们彼此都变得更加重要了一点。

sentences.en: And you both are undeniably human.
sentences.zh: 你们两个都无可否认地是人类。

sentences.en: Perhaps human evolution means becoming more human.
sentences.zh: 也许人类的进化意味着变得更具人性。

sentences.en: And the discovery of the amount of room in the human heart is our next great discovery.
sentences.zh: 而发现人类心中还有多少空间，将是我们下一次伟大的发现。

sentences.en: There is a complexity to that that is very affecting.
sentences.zh: 其中蕴含着一种非常触动人心的复杂性。

sentences.en: Thank you, sir.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，先生。

sentences.en: I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Appreciate the kind words.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的美言。

sentences.en: Yeah, I hadn't seen that one on your blog.
sentences.zh: 对，我没在你的博客上见过那一首。

sentences.en: Is that an older one?
sentences.zh: 那是旧作吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: It's ancient.
sentences.zh: 它太古老了。

sentences.en: February 11th.
sentences.zh: 2月11日的。

sentences.en: It's an old timer.
sentences.zh: 是个老古董了。

sentences.en: Would you like another one?
sentences.zh: 你想再听一首吗？

sentences.en: Or am I going to get more of you?
sentences.zh: 还是说你想多听听我说话？

sentences.en: No, no, please.
sentences.zh: 不，不，请继续。

sentences.en: And say the website, too, so people can make sure they can find you everywhere that you are.
sentences.zh: 也顺便说一下网址，好让大家确保能在你能出现的各个地方找到你。

sentences.en: Very hard to find.
sentences.zh: 很难找。

sentences.en: It's jfbeerline.com.
sentences.zh: It's jfbeerline.com.

sentences.en: But now, since my name is not quite phonetic in English, it's B-I-E-R-L-E-I-N.
sentences.zh: 但现在，由于我的名字在英语中发音不太符合拼写规则，它是 B-I-E-R-L-E-I-N。

sentences.en: And since I'm a great lover of gardening and wine, I've planted lots of grapes.
sentences.zh: 而且由于我非常热爱园艺和葡萄酒，我种了许多葡萄。

sentences.en: And I wrote a poem about it called Dormant.
sentences.zh: 我为此写了一首诗，叫《休眠》（Dormant）。

sentences.en: I just love that word.
